tasks.title: Vending Machine Cycle Timer
tasks.prompt:
A vending machine dispenses items with a fixed mechanical cycle. The machine performs a sequence of operations for each row of a batch. The batch data is: 
Row 1: item code 'A1', cycle time 12 seconds, quantity 5.
Row 2: item code 'B3', cycle time 9 seconds, quantity 8.
Row 3: item code 'C2', cycle time 15 seconds, quantity 4.
Row 4: item code 'D4', cycle time 7 seconds, quantity 6.
Row 5: item code 'E1', cycle time 11 seconds, quantity 3.

For each row, compute the total dispense time in seconds (cycle time * quantity). Then compute the total for the entire batch in both seconds and minutes (minutes as a Real rounded to 2 decimal places).

Print exactly 7 lines in this format:
Batch Total Seconds: <total_seconds>
Batch Total Minutes: <total_minutes_real>
Row <index> <item_code> <row_seconds>
Row <index> <item_code> <row_seconds>
Row <index> <item_code> <row_seconds>
Row <index> <item_code> <row_seconds>
Row <index> <item_code> <row_seconds>

Where <index> is 1 through 5, <item_code> is the code string, <row_seconds> is the integer seconds for that row, <total_seconds> is the sum of all row seconds, and <total_minutes_real> is the total seconds divided by 60 formatted to 2 decimal places. No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: date-free calendar and time arithmetic in minutes and seconds (no real dates, no leap years)

tasks.title: Ferry Crossing Schedule
tasks.prompt:
A ferry service lists scheduled crossing durations for today's route. The schedule is given as an array of crossing times in minutes: [45, 52, 38, 61, 47, 55, 40].

The service wants a summary report. Compute the total time for all crossings, the number of crossings, the average crossing time (Real rounded to 2 decimal places), and the longest crossing time.

Print exactly 5 lines in this format:
Total Minutes: <total>
Crossing Count: <count>
Average Minutes: <average>
Longest Crossing: <longest>
Total Hours Minutes: <hours>h <mins>m

Where <total> is the sum of the array, <count> is the array length, <average> is the total divided by count formatted to 2 decimal places, <longest> is the maximum value, and <hours> and <mins> are the integer hours and remaining minutes when <total> minutes is converted to hours and minutes. No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: date-free calendar and time arithmetic in minutes and seconds (no real dates, no leap years)

Washer 3: 40 minutes

Dryer 3: <seconds>s
Washer 1: <seconds>s
Washer 2: <seconds>s
Washer 3: <seconds>s

Total Minutes: <total_minutes>
Average Seconds: <avg_seconds>

Total Minutes: <total_minutes>

tasks.title: Warehouse Shift Duration Tally
tasks.prompt:
A warehouse logs shift durations in minutes for its staff. The records are: [240, 315, 270, 180, 330, 225, 285].

Compute the total minutes worked across all shifts, convert that total to hours and minutes, count how many shifts exceeded 4 hours (240 minutes), and find the shortest shift.

Total Minutes: <total>
Total Hours: <hours>
Remaining Minutes: <rem_minutes>
Shifts Over 4h: <count_over>
Shortest Shift: <shortest>
Average Minutes: <avg>

tasks.title: Greenhouse Plant Care Summary
tasks.prompt:
You are checking a JSON record of plants in a greenhouse. The record contains a list of plants, each with a name, a watering interval in days, and an optional sun requirement.

Given the following JSON document:

{
  "plants": [
    {"name": "Tomato", "water_days": 2, "sun": "full"},
    {"name": "Basil", "water_days": 3, "sun": "partial"},
    {"name": "Fern", "water_days": 1, "sun": "shade"},
    {"name": "Cactus", "water_days": 14, "sun": "full"},
    {"name": "Mint", "water_days": 4}
  ]
}

Write a program that prints a care summary. Print each plant on its own line in the format:

name | water every N days | sun

where N is the watering interval and sun is the sun requirement, or "any" if the sun field is missing. After listing all plants, print a blank line, then print the total number of plants on a line labeled exactly:

Total plants: N

Finally, print the number of plants that need watering more often than every 3 days (strictly less than 3) on a line labeled exactly:

Frequent waterers: N

Output format example (illustrative only, not the answer):
Name | water every N days | sun
Name2 | water every N days | sun

Total plants: N
Frequent waterers: N

Ensure no trailing spaces on any line.
tasks.category: processing a small JSON document given inline (nested objects and arrays; totals, lookups with defaults, filtering, missing keys)

After all fruit lines, print a blank line, then print the overall total weight across all baskets on a line labeled exactly:

M3:      13      10      12

Each stove's total time is the sum of times for meals assigned to it. The kitchen finishes when the slowest stove finishes. Find the assignment of all 4 meals to stoves (each stove 0-2 meals) that minimizes the maximum total time across stoves. Report that minimum possible maximum time.

tasks.title: Orchard Sorting Belt State Machine
tasks.prompt:
You are monitoring a conveyor belt at an orchard packing house. Apples arrive one by one and are sorted into three crates: A (Red Delicious), B (Gala), and C (Granny Smith). A small machine reads the label of each apple and advances a state counter.

The machine starts in state 0. For each apple label read, it transitions as follows:
- From state 0: if the label is A, go to state 1; if B, go to state 2; if C, go to state 3.
- From state 1: if the label is A, stay in state 1; if B, go to state 4; if C, go to state 3.
- From state 2: if the label is A, go to state 1; if B, stay in state 2; if C, go to state 5.
- From state 3: if the label is A, go to state 4; if B, go to state 5; if C, stay in state 3.
- From state 4: if the label is A, go to state 6; if B, go to state 6; if C, go to state 6.
- From state 5: if the label is A, go to state 6; if B, go to state 6; if C, go to state 6.
- From state 6: stay in state 6 regardless of the label.

The belt carries the following sequence of 10 apples: A, B, A, C, B, C, A, A, B, C

Write a program that simulates this state machine and prints the state after each apple is processed.

Output format: exactly 10 lines. Each line is the word "State" followed by a space, then the integer state number, then a space, then the label of the apple just processed. For example, after the first apple (A), the output line is: State 1 A

No trailing spaces on any line.

tasks.title: Board Game Dice Turn Tracker
tasks.prompt:
In a simple board game, a player rolls a die and moves a token around a track. The game tracks the player's turn status using a small state machine.

- 3: Bonus

- From state 1: if the roll is 1 or 2, go to state 2; if the roll is 3, 4, or 5, go to state 2; if the roll is 6, go to state 3.
- From state 2: if the roll is 6, go to state 3; otherwise go to state 0.
- From state 3: go to state 0 regardless of the roll.

The player rolls the following sequence of 9 values: 3, 6, 2, 1, 5, 6, 4, 2, 6

Write a program that simulates the state machine and prints the state name after each roll.

Output format: exactly 9 lines. Each line has the form: Roll <n> -> <StateName>
where <n> is the roll number (1 through 9) and <StateName> is exactly one of Waiting, Moving, Landing, or Bonus.

No trailing spaces on any line.

tasks.title: Library Book Checkout State Machine
tasks.prompt:

- 3: FeeDue

Transitions:
- From state 0: if member is P, go to state 2; if member is S, go to state 1.
- From state 1: if condition is N, go to state 3; if condition is U, go to state 1.
- From state 2: if condition is N, go to state 3; if condition is U, go to state 4.
- From state 3: if member is P, go to state 4; if member is S, go to state 0.
- From state 4: go to state 0 regardless.

The queue of 8 requests (member, condition) is: (S,N), (P,U), (S,U), (P,N), (S,N), (P,U), (S,U), (P,N)

Write a program that simulates this and prints the fee code after each request. The fee code is the state number mapped as: 0 -> NONE, 1 -> STD, 2 -> PREM, 3 -> DUE, 4 -> FREE.

Output format: exactly 8 lines. Each line: Request <i>: <CODE>
where <i> is 1 through 8 and <CODE> is one of NONE, STD, PREM, DUE, FREE.

No trailing spaces.

tasks.title: Warehouse Scanner State Machine
tasks.prompt:
A handheld scanner at a warehouse moves pallets through a checkpoint. It reads a zone letter and a weight class digit for each pallet, advancing a state.

For each pallet, the scanner reads zone Z in {A,B,C} and class D in {1,2}.

Transitions:
- From state 0: if Z=A go to 1; if Z=B go to 2; if Z=C go to 3.
- From state 1: if D=1 go to 4; if D=2 go to 2.
- From state 2: if D=1 go to 3; if D=2 go to 4.

tasks.title: Bakery Oven Temperature Controller
tasks.prompt:
A bakery oven controller uses a state machine to decide heating behavior based on sensor readings. Each reading is a temperature in Celsius and a door flag (0=closed, 1=open).

Start at state 0.

Transitions (given current state, temperature T, door flag D):
- From 0: if D=0 and T<180 go to 1; else stay 0.
- From 1: if T>=180 and D=0 go to 2; if D=1 go to 4; else stay 1.
- From 2: if T<160 go to 3; if D=1 go to 4; else stay 2.
- From 3: if T>=160 and D=0 go to 2; else stay 3.
- From 4: if D=0 go to 1; else stay 4.

The sensor log of 9 readings (T, D) is: (150,0), (170,0), (190,0), (195,0), (155,0), (165,1), (170,1), (175,0), (185,0)

where <i> is 1..9 and <STATE> is one of Off, Preheat, Bake, Hold, DoorOpen.

No trailing spaces.

tasks.title: Board Game Card Play Sequence

- From 2: if R=1 go to 3; if R=2 go to 2; if R=3 go to 4.
- From 3: if C=R go to 4; if C=G go to 1.
- From 4: go to 0 regardless.

3. Prints exactly 5 lines, one per station, each in the format:
"Station N: pour=Ds rest=Gs"
where N is the station number (1 through 5), D is that station's pour duration in seconds, and G is the rest gap after that station. For the last station (Station 5), G is the time from its finish until second 360, so compute G = 360 minus its finish time.

tasks.title: Warehouse Pallet Weight Check
tasks.prompt:
A warehouse records pallets awaiting shipment. The file `pallets.txt` has one record per line with three space-separated fields: pallet ID (text, no spaces), weight in kilograms (integer), max allowed weight (integer, always positive).

Write a program that reads the file and prints a validation report.

Rules:
- A pallet is "OVER" if weight exceeds max allowed; otherwise it is "SAFE".
- A pallet is "BAD" if weight is negative (these are counted as BAD and not classified as OVER or SAFE).

Output exactly these lines, in file order:
- For each pallet: pallet ID, a space, classification ("OVER", "SAFE", or "BAD"), a space, weight as integer.
- Then one line: "Over count: " followed by number of OVER pallets.
- Then one line: "Bad count: " followed by number of BAD pallets.
- Then one line: "Safe total kg: " followed by the sum of weights of all SAFE pallets.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: reading a small text data file provided with the exercise, one record per line (parse fields, validate, summarise)

tasks.title: Orchard Tree Yield Tracker
tasks.prompt:
An orchard records expected yield per tree. The file `tree_yield.txt` has one record per line with three space-separated fields: tree ID (text, no spaces), variety (text, no spaces), expected yield in kilograms (integer).

Write a program that reads the file and prints a summary.

Rules:
- A tree is "high" if expected yield is strictly greater than 100; otherwise it is "normal".
- Negative yields are invalid; count them separately and do not classify them as high or normal.

Output exactly these lines:
- For each valid tree in file order: tree ID, a space, variety, a space, the classification ("high" or "normal").
- Then one line: "High count: " followed by number of high trees.
- Then one line: "Normal count: " followed by number of normal trees.
- Then one line: "Invalid count: " followed by number of invalid records.
- Then one line: "Varieties: " followed by the number of distinct variety names among valid records.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: reading a small text data file provided with the exercise, one record per line (parse fields, validate, summarise)

files.tree_yield.txt:
T1 apple 150
T2 pear 80
T3 plum 120
T4 cherry 60
T5 apple 200
T6 pear -10
T7 plum 110
T8 apple 90

tasks.title: Bike-Share Dock Station Balance
tasks.prompt:
A bike-share system logs dock counts. The file `dock_status.txt` has one record per line with three space-separated fields: station name (text, no spaces), bikes available (integer), empty docks available (integer).

Write a program that reads the file and prints a status report.

Rules:
- Capacity for a station is bikes available plus empty docks available.
- A station is "EMPTY" if bikes available is 0.
- A station is "FULL" if empty docks available is 0 (and bikes available is not 0).
- A station is "BALANCED" otherwise.

Output exactly these lines:
- For each station in file order: station name, a space, status ("EMPTY", "FULL", or "BALANCED"), a space, capacity as integer.
- Then one line: "Empty: " followed by number of EMPTY stations.
- Then one line: "Full: " followed by number of FULL stations.
- Then one line: "Balanced: " followed by number of BALANCED stations.
- Then one line: "Total bikes: " followed by sum of bikes available across all stations.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: reading a small text data file provided with the exercise, one record per line (parse fields, validate, summarise)

Central 12 8
North 0 20
South 18 0
East 10 10
West 5 15

tasks.title: Warehouse Shipment Route Check
tasks.prompt:
A warehouse logs outgoing shipments. The file `shipments.txt` has one record per line with three space-separated fields: shipment ID (text, no spaces), destination zone (text, no spaces), package count (integer).

Write a program that reads the file and prints a routing report.

Rules:
- Zone A and Zone B are "local"; all other zones are "remote".
- A shipment is "HEAVY" if package count is strictly greater than 50; otherwise it is "LIGHT".
- Negative package counts are invalid; count them and do not classify.

Output exactly these lines:
- For each valid shipment in file order: shipment ID, a space, distance class ("local" or "remote"), a space, weight class ("HEAVY" or "LIGHT").
- Then one line: "Local heavy: " followed by count of local HEAVY shipments.
- Then one line: "Remote light: " followed by count of remote LIGHT shipments.
- Then one line: "Invalid: " followed by count of invalid records.
- Then one line: "Total packages: " followed by sum of package counts for valid records.

No trailing spaces.

tasks.title: Orchard Frost Risk Log
tasks.prompt:
An orchard records overnight temperatures to assess frost risk. The file `frost_log.txt` has one record per line with three space-separated fields: block label (text, no spaces), minimum temperature in degrees Celsius (integer), wind speed in km/h (integer).

Write a program that reads the file and prints a risk report.

Rules:
- A reading is "FROST" if minimum temperature is strictly below 0.
- A reading is "WINDY" if wind speed is strictly greater than 30 (checked only for non-FROST readings).
- Otherwise the reading is "SAFE".
- Invalid if minimum temperature is below -50 or wind speed is negative; count these separately and do not classify.

Output exactly these lines:
- For each valid reading in file order: block label, a space, classification ("FROST", "WINDY", or "SAFE").
- Then one line: "Frost blocks: " followed by count of FROST readings.
- Then one line: "Wind blocks: " followed by count of WINDY readings.
- Then one line: "Safe blocks: " followed by count of SAFE readings.
- Then one line: "Invalid readings: " followed by count of invalid readings.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: reading a small text data file provided with the exercise, one record per line (parse fields, validate, summarise)

    {"sensor": "T2", "temp": 26.8, "humidity": 58.7, "ok": true},

    {"sensor": "T5", "temp": 27.6, "humidity": 55.1, "ok": true}
  ]
}

Write a program that reads this JSON (embedded as a literal string in your code), extracts the readings, and prints a formatted table to standard output.

Output format (exactly, line by line):
Line 1: Zone A Sensor Readings
Line 2: (empty line)
Line 3: Sensor  Temp(C)  Humidity(%)  Status

No trailing spaces on any line.

tasks.title: Marathon Aid Station Snack Combinations
tasks.prompt:

tasks.title: Parking Garage Floor Paths
tasks.prompt:

tasks.title: Train Network Ticket Code Validator
tasks.prompt:
A train network issues tickets with a five-digit code. The network wants to validate each ticket code before printing.

A ticket code is valid if all of the following hold:

- The 3rd digit is greater than the 2nd digit.
- The digits are strictly increasing from the 4th to the 5th position.

Here are the five ticket codes to check:

14375
25416
36729
48257
59648

For each code, in the order given, print a line with the code, a space, and either OK or REJECT.
After all five lines, print one final line: the count of valid codes followed by a space and the word valid.

Output format (example of one line): 14375 OK
Final line format: 2 valid
No trailing spaces.

tasks.prompt:

No trailing spaces.

tasks.title: Aquarium Tank Label Check

labels = ["A1-12", "B3-45", "C2-07", "D4-88", "E1-56", "F5-33"]

For each label, validate it:

- The second character must be a digit from 1 to 9.
- The third character must be '-'.
- The fourth and fifth characters must be digits.

or
Label: XYZ -> INVALID

where XYZ is the original label, Z is the zone letter, and NN is the tank number zero-padded to 2 digits. After all labels, print:

where N is the count of valid labels and M is the total number of labels (6).

tasks.title: Recipe Book Spice Code Check
tasks.prompt:
A recipe book uses spice codes of the form CCC-NNN where CCC is a three-letter abbreviation and NNN is a three-digit quantity in milligrams. The codes are:

For each code:

- If quantity >= 200, mark as "High".
- If 100 <= quantity < 200, mark as "Medium".
- If quantity < 100, mark as "Low".

Print 6 lines:

Exact format:
ABBREV: QQQ mg -> LEVEL

where ABBREV is the uppercase three-letter code, QQQ is the quantity as printed (preserving leading zeros, e.g. 075), and LEVEL is High, Medium, or Low.

After the 6 lines, print:

where NNN is the sum of all quantities (as a plain integer with no leading zeros).

tasks.prompt:

tasks.title: Lighthouse Lamp Fuel Log
tasks.prompt:
A lighthouse keeper manages the lamp fuel using a circular ring buffer of 4 tanks. Each tank holds a number of litres. Operations are applied in order, and after each operation the ring buffer state is printed.

The ring buffer starts with tanks holding: 12, 0, 7, 5 litres. A pointer marks the current tank, starting at index 0 (the first tank).

Operations (applied in order):
1. FILL — add 6 litres to the tank at the pointer, then advance the pointer by 1 (wrapping around).
2. BURN — remove 4 litres from the tank at the pointer (if the tank has fewer than 4, it becomes 0), then advance the pointer by 1.
3. FILL — add 6 litres to the tank at the pointer, then advance the pointer by 1.
4. SKIP — do nothing to any tank, do not move the pointer.
5. BURN — remove 4 litres from the tank at the pointer, then advance the pointer by 1.
6. FILL — add 6 litres to the tank at the pointer, then advance the pointer by 1.

After EACH of the 6 operations, print one line:
`T <op_number> : <t0> <t1> <t2> <t3> | P <pointer>`
where `<op_number>` is 1 through 6, `<t0>`..`<t3>` are the current litres in tanks 0..3 (as integers), and `<pointer>` is the current pointer index (0..3).

After all operations, print one final line:
`TOTAL <sum>`
where `<sum>` is the total litres across all 4 tanks.

No trailing spaces on any line.

- `PEEK` — look at the top book without removing it.

POP

PEEK
PUSH Drift
POP
PUSH Kites
POP
PUSH Moss
PEEK
POP
POP

After each operation, print exactly one line describing the result:
- For `PUSH`: `PUSHED <title> SIZE <n>` where `<n>` is the stack size after the push.
- For `POP`: `POPPED <title> SIZE <n>` where `<title>` is the removed book and `<n>` is the stack size after the pop. If the stack was empty, print `POPPED - SIZE 0` instead.
- For `PEEK`: `TOP <title> SIZE <n>` where `<title>` is the current top book. If the stack was empty, print `TOP - SIZE 0` instead.

After all operations, print one final line:
`FINAL <n> : <title1> <title2> ...`
where `<n>` is the final stack size and the titles are listed from top to bottom, separated by single spaces. If the stack is empty, print `FINAL 0 : -`.

If it has fewer, remove it and continue burning the next pellet with the remainder (if the queue empties before the burn time is used up, the remaining burn time is simply lost).
- `SKIP` — do nothing.

The operations, in order:

LOAD 5
LOAD 3
BURN 4
LOAD 7
BURN 3
SKIP
BURN 6
LOAD 2
BURN 5
BURN 4

After EACH operation, print one line:
`<op_number> : <remaining1>,<remaining2>,...`
where `<op_number>` is the operation index (1-based), and the numbers are the remaining burn minutes of each pellet in the queue from front to back, separated by commas with no spaces. If the queue is empty, print just `<op_number> : -`.

- For `TOPDIFF`: `DIFF <d> DEPTH <n>` where `<d>` is the computed difference and `<n>` is the current depth. If fewer than 2 readings are on the stack, print `DIFF - DEPTH <n>` instead.

tasks.title: Aquarium Filter Maintenance Timer
tasks.prompt:
An aquarium has 3 tanks, each with a filter that must be cleaned after a fixed interval. Cleaning takes a fixed service time. Given the initial service times and a total operating window, determine when each filter next needs cleaning within the window and count how many cleanings occur for each tank.

Input data:
FilterInterval = [7, 5, 9]
ServiceTime = 1
Window = 20

Output format (exactly 4 lines, no trailing spaces):
Tank 1 cleanings: 3
Tank 2 cleanings: 4
Tank 3 cleanings: 2
Total cleanings: 9
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Beekeeper Smoke Puff Timing
tasks.prompt:
A beekeeper puffs smoke at a hive on a timer. Puffs occur at fixed intervals, but each puff takes a fixed duration during which the beekeeper cannot start the next puff. Given the puff interval (start-to-start if no duration), puff duration, and a total time budget, compute how many puffs complete and the time of the last puff's start.

Input data:
PuffInterval = 5
PuffDuration = 2
Budget = 30

Output format (exactly 2 lines, no trailing spaces):
Puffs completed: 6
Last puff start: 25
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Print Shop Ink Cartridge Changeover
tasks.prompt:
A print shop printer uses ink cartridges that last a fixed number of pages. Each cartridge change takes a fixed number of minutes. Given a list of print jobs (each with a page count), simulate the printing: track pages printed on the current cartridge, change cartridge when it runs out (the changeover time pauses printing). Report total changeovers and total changeover minutes.

Input data:
CartridgeCapacity = 50
ChangeoverMinutes = 3
Jobs = [20, 35, 15, 40, 10, 30]

Output format (exactly 2 lines, no trailing spaces):
Cartridge changeovers: 4
Total changeover minutes: 12
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: School Cafeteria Tray Line Timer
tasks.prompt:
Students form a single line at a cafeteria tray station. Each student takes a fixed service time. A student who arrives after the line is empty starts immediately upon arrival; otherwise they join the queue. Given arrival times and service times, compute when each student is served and report the maximum wait time (service start minus arrival).

Input data:
Arrivals = [0, 1, 3, 4, 8]
Service  = [2, 3, 1, 4, 2]

Output format (exactly 3 lines, no trailing spaces):
Student 2 served at: 6
Student 4 served at: 11
Max wait: 3
tasks.category: scheduling and simulation with a fixed timeline of events (queues, timers, resource use)

tasks.title: Robot Grid Path Checker
tasks.prompt:
A small robot moves on a 5x5 grid of tiles. The robot starts at the top-left tile (row 1, column 1) and must reach the bottom-right tile (row 5, column 5). A path is a sequence of moves, each either 'R' (one tile right) or 'D' (one tile down). A path is valid if it never goes outside the grid.

Three candidate paths are given as text:
Path A: "RRDDDRDD"
Path B: "DDRRDDRR"
Path C: "DRDDRRDDDR"

Write a program that checks each path and reports whether it is valid (stays within the grid) and whether it lands exactly on the goal tile.

Output exactly 4 lines in this format, with no trailing spaces:
Path A: valid=1 goal=0
Path B: valid=1 goal=1
Path C: valid=0 goal=0
Summary: valid=2 goal=1
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Bakery Order Combinations
tasks.prompt:
A bakery offers 4 types of pastries: croissant, scone, muffin, danish. A customer picks exactly 3 items, and the same type may be chosen more than once (order does not matter).

For example, choosing 2 croissants and 1 scone counts as one distinct combination.

Write a program that counts the total number of distinct combinations of exactly 3 pastries (with repetition allowed, order not mattering).

Output exactly 2 lines, with no trailing spaces:
Pastries: 4
Combinations: 20
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Fitness Log Weekly Streak
tasks.prompt:
A fitness log records whether a person worked out each day for 7 days (Monday through Sunday). The log is given as:
Mon: yes
Tue: yes
Wed: no
Thu: yes
Fri: yes
Sat: yes
Sun: no

A streak is a maximal consecutive run of 'yes' days. Write a program that finds the longest streak and reports its length and the starting day.

Output exactly 3 lines, with no trailing spaces:
Streak count: 3
Longest streak: 3
Start day: Thu
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Warehouse Bin Permutations
tasks.prompt:
A warehouse has 4 bins labeled A, B, C, D. A picker must visit exactly 3 bins in a specific order (the same bin may appear more than once in a sequence, and order matters).

For example, A-B-A is a valid sequence of length 3.

Write a program that counts the total number of distinct sequences of length 3 using these 4 bins.

Output exactly 2 lines, with no trailing spaces:
Bins: 4
Sequences of length 3: 64
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Library Book Shelf Arrangements
tasks.prompt:
A librarian is arranging 5 books on a shelf. The books have heights (in cm): 22, 18, 25, 20, 24. A valid arrangement is one where no book is taller than the book immediately to its left (i.e., heights are non-increasing from left to right).

Write a program that counts how many of the 5! = 120 permutations of these 5 books form a valid arrangement.

Output exactly 2 lines, with no trailing spaces:
Total permutations: 120
Valid arrangements: 1
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Warehouse Shelf Subsets
tasks.prompt:
A warehouse shelf holds 6 boxes labeled 1 through 6. A worker selects a subset of boxes to move. The subset must contain at least 2 boxes and at most 4 boxes.

Write a program that counts how many distinct subsets satisfy this rule.

Output exactly 2 lines, with no trailing spaces:
Boxes: 6
Subsets (size 2 to 4): 50
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Bakery Display Combinations
tasks.prompt:
A bakery display has 3 shelves. Each shelf can hold one of 3 cake types: chocolate, vanilla, or red velvet. Two displays are considered different if any shelf holds a different cake type.

Write a program that counts how many distinct displays are possible.

Output exactly 2 lines, with no trailing spaces:
Shelves: 3
Cake types: 3
Displays: 27
tasks.category: small combinatorics and recursion (generating or counting arrangements of a few items)

tasks.title: Garden Plot Sunlight Hours
tasks.prompt:
A community garden has three plots (Plot A, Plot B, Plot C) each growing three types of plants: Tomatoes, Herbs, and Flowers. The average daily sunlight hours each plant type receives in each plot are recorded in a 3x3 matrix:

Plot A: Tomatoes 6.5, Herbs 5.0, Flowers 7.5
Plot B: Tomatoes 4.0, Herbs 6.0, Flowers 3.5
Plot C: Tomatoes 5.5, Herbs 4.5, Flowers 6.0

Plants need at least 5.0 hours of sunlight to be classified as "Thriving". Plants receiving less than 5.0 hours are classified as "Struggling".

Write a program that analyzes the garden and prints a report.

Output format:
First, for each plot (in the order Plot A, Plot B, Plot C), print one line: the plot name, a colon, a space, then the classification for Tomatoes, Herbs, and Flowers in that order separated by single spaces (using exactly the words "Thriving" or "Struggling").
Then print a blank line.
Then print one line for each plant type (Tomatoes, Herbs, Flowers in that order): the plant name, a colon, a space, then the total sunlight hours across all three plots formatted with exactly 1 decimal place.

Example of line format (not the expected answer): "Plot A: Thriving Thriving Thriving"
tasks.category: matrix operations on small fixed matrices

tasks.title: Print Shop Ink Coverage Grid
tasks.prompt:
A print shop tracks ink coverage (in milliliters) used per page for three printers (Printer A, Printer B, Printer C) across three ink colors (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow). The data is a 3x3 matrix:

Printer A: Cyan 12.4, Magenta 8.6, Yellow 6.2
Printer B: Cyan 9.8, Magenta 11.3, Yellow 7.5
Printer C: Cyan 7.1, Magenta 6.9, Yellow 10.4

An ink color is flagged as "overuse" at a printer if its coverage at that printer exceeds 10.0 ml.

Write a program that analyzes the coverage and prints a report.

Output format:
First, for each printer (in order), print one line: the printer name, a colon, a space, then the total ink across all three colors formatted with exactly 1 decimal place.
Then print a blank line.
Then print one line for each ink color (Cyan, Magenta, Yellow in that order): the color name, a colon, a space, then the number of printers where that color was flagged as overuse, followed by a space and the word "overuse" if that count is greater than zero, or "no overuse" if the count is zero. (So the line reads e.g. "Cyan: 1 overuse" or "Magenta: 0 no overuse").

Example of line format (not the expected answer): "Printer A: 27.2"
tasks.category: matrix operations on small fixed matrices

tasks.title: Bike Share Weather Impact Grid
tasks.prompt:
A bike-share operator records the number of trips taken at three stations (Central, Harbor, Uptown) during three weather conditions (Sunny, Rainy, Windy). The trip counts are in a 3x3 matrix:

Central: Sunny 320, Rainy 95, Windy 210
Harbor: Sunny 275, Rainy 140, Windy 185
Uptown: Sunny 410, Rainy 60, Windy 250

Rainy-day ridership is considered "low" at a station if rainy trips are less than 40% of sunny trips at that station, otherwise "normal".

Write a program that analyzes the ridership and prints a report.

Output format:
First, for each station (in order), print one line: the station name, a colon, a space, then the rainy-day classification (the word "low" or "normal").
Then print a blank line.
Then print one line for each weather condition (Sunny, Rainy, Windy in that order): the condition name, a colon, a space, then the total trips across all three stations.
Then print one final line: "Overall: " followed by the overall average trips per cell across all nine cells, formatted with exactly 1 decimal place.

Example of line format (not the expected answer): "Central: low"
tasks.category: matrix operations on small fixed matrices

tasks.title: Garden Irrigation Schedule Matrix
tasks.prompt:
A garden has three zones (North, South, East) each containing three beds (Bed 1, Bed 2, Bed 3). The number of minutes of watering each bed needs per week is recorded in a 3x3 matrix:

North: Bed 1 = 30, Bed 2 = 45, Bed 3 = 20
South: Bed 1 = 50, Bed 2 = 35, Bed 3 = 40
East: Bed 1 = 25, Bed 2 = 55, Bed 3 = 15

A bed is classified as "heavy" if it needs 40 minutes or more, otherwise "light".

Write a program that analyzes the schedule and prints a report.

Output format:
First, for each zone (in order), print one line: the zone name, a colon, a space, then the classification for Bed 1, Bed 2, and Bed 3 in that order separated by single spaces (using exactly the words "heavy" or "light").
Then print a blank line.
Then print one line for each bed number (Bed 1, Bed 2, Bed 3 in that order): "Bed N: " followed by the total minutes for that bed across all three zones, then a space, then the word "heavy" if that total is 100 minutes or more, otherwise the word "light".

Example of line format (not the expected answer): "North: light heavy light"
tasks.category: matrix operations on small fixed matrices

tasks.title: Fitness Log Weight Progress
tasks.prompt:
A fitness log records body weight (in kg) at three check-ins (Week 1, Week 4, Week 8) for three people (Alex, Blake, Casey). The weights are in a 3x3 matrix:

Alex: Week 1 = 82.5, Week 4 = 80.3, Week 8 = 78.1
Blake: Week 1 = 65.0, Week 4 = 66.2, Week 8 = 64.8
Casey: Week 1 = 90.0, Week 4 = 88.5, Week 8 = 87.0

A person's progress is classified as "improving" if their Week 8 weight is lower than their Week 1 weight, otherwise "maintaining".

Write a program that analyzes the log and prints a report.

Output format:
First, for each person (in order), print one line: the person's name, a colon, a space, then their progress classification (the word "improving" or "maintaining").
Then print a blank line.
Then print one line for each check-in (Week 1, Week 4, Week 8 in that order): "Week N: " followed by the average weight across all three people at that check-in, formatted with exactly 2 decimal places.
Then print one final line: "Total Change: " followed by the sum of the absolute differences between Week 1 and Week 8 for all three people, formatted with exactly 2 decimal place.

Example of line format (not the expected answer): "Alex: improving"
tasks.category: matrix operations on small fixed matrices

tasks.title: Marathon Split Time Analysis
tasks.prompt:
A marathon runner records their split times (in minutes) at the 10 km, 20 km, and 30 km marks for three different races (Race A, Race B, Race C). The splits are in a 3x3 matrix:

Race A: 10 km = 52, 20 km = 55, 30 km = 58
Race B: 10 km = 48, 20 km = 51, 30 km = 57
Race C: 10 km = 50, 20 km = 54, 30 km = 56

A split is flagged as "fast" if it is 51 minutes or less, otherwise "steady".

Write a program that analyzes the splits and prints a report.

Output format:
First, for each race (in order), print one line: the race name, a colon, a space, then the flag for the 10 km, 20 km, and 30 km splits in that order separated by single spaces (using exactly the words "fast" or "steady").
Then print a blank line.
Then print one line for each distance (10 km, 20 km, 30 km in that order): "10 km: " followed by the total minutes across all three races for that distance, then a space, then the word "fast" if that total is 155 minutes or less, otherwise the word "steady".

Example of line format (not the expected answer): "Race A: fast steady steady"
tasks.category: matrix operations on small fixed matrices

tasks.title: Weather Station Rain Gauge Reset Counter
tasks.prompt:
You are maintaining a simple weather station that tracks rainfall. The station records a sequence of readings over 10 minutes. Each reading is either a new rainfall amount in millimeters or a reset command (0). The gauge accumulates rainfall until a reset command appears, at which point it prints the total for the period and starts a new accumulation.

The input sequence of readings (in order) is:
1.5, 0.3, 2.1, 0, 0.7, 1.2, 0, 0.4, 0.9, 0

Write a program that processes this sequence. Every time a reset command (0) appears, output a line in the exact format:
Period total: X.XX
where X.XX is the accumulated rainfall for that period with exactly 2 decimal places.

After processing all readings, output one final line:
Final total: X.XX
where X.XX is the sum of all period totals with exactly 2 decimal places.

Output exactly 4 lines with no trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Marathon Checkpoint Gate Counter
tasks.prompt:
A marathon has 12 checkpoints. Each checkpoint logs a runner's bib number as they pass. The race organizer wants to count how many distinct runners complete each 4-checkpoint segment (segment 1: checkpoints 1-4, segment 2: checkpoints 5-8, segment 3: checkpoints 9-12).

The sequence of bib numbers passing checkpoints 1 through 12 (in order) is:
101, 102, 101, 103, 102, 104, 103, 104, 105, 101, 105, 106

A runner is counted in a segment if they appear at least once in that segment's checkpoint sequence. Write a program that outputs, for each segment, a line in the exact format:
Segment N: X runners
where N is the segment number (1, 2, or 3) and X is the count of distinct runners in that segment.

Output exactly 3 lines with no trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: School Timetable Bell Ring Sequence
tasks.prompt:
A school's bell system rings to mark transitions between periods. Each bell event is either a ring (1) or silence (0). When two rings occur with exactly one silence between them, it marks a double-period block. Count how many double-period blocks occur.

The sequence of 12 bell events (in order) is:
1, 0, 1, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 0, 1, 1, 0

A double-period block is defined as the pattern: ring, silence, ring (i.e., events at positions i, i+1, i+2 where they are 1, 0, 1). Overlapping patterns count separately.

Write a program that outputs exactly one line in the format:
Double periods: X
where X is the total count of such patterns.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Print Shop Paper Tray Refill Cycle
tasks.prompt:
A print shop's printer has a paper tray that starts with 500 sheets. Each job consumes a known number of sheets. When the tray would drop below 100 sheets, the operator refills it to 500 before the next job. Track how many refills occur.

The sequence of job sheet requirements (in order) is:
80, 120, 90, 75, 110, 95, 85, 105, 70, 95

Rules:
- Process jobs in order.
- Before running a job, if current sheets minus job requirement would be less than 100, add a refill: set sheets to 500, and increment refill count by 1.
- Then subtract the job requirement from sheets.

Write a program that outputs exactly two lines:
Refills: X
Remaining: Y
where X is the number of refills and Y is the final sheet count.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Weather Station Wind Direction Segment
tasks.prompt:
A weather station records wind direction as compass degrees at 12 consecutive readings. The station classifies each reading as N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, or NW based on the nearest 45-degree sector (e.g., 0-22 = N, 23-67 = NE, etc.; 338-360 = N).

The 12 readings (in degrees) are:
10, 50, 95, 140, 175, 220, 265, 310, 350, 20, 60, 100

Write a program that classifies each reading, then outputs exactly 4 lines:
First: D
Last: D
Max consecutive same: X
Changed: Y
where D is the compass letter (N, NE, E, SE, S, SW, W, or NW), X is the length of the longest run of identical classifications, and Y is the number of times the classification changes between consecutive readings.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Marathon Water Station Cup Count
tasks.prompt:
A marathon water station records cups handed out at 10 intervals. The station starts with 300 cups. After each interval, if remaining cups fall below 100, a volunteer restocks by 200 cups. Track total cups distributed and restocks.

The cups handed out at each of the 10 intervals (in order) are:
40, 35, 50, 45, 30, 55, 40, 35, 50, 45

Rules:
- Process intervals in order.
- Subtract cups handed out from remaining.
- After subtraction, if remaining < 100, add 200 to remaining and increment restock count by 1.

Write a program that outputs exactly three lines:
Total handed out: X
Restocks: Y
Remaining: Z
where X is the sum of all cups handed out, Y is the number of restocks, and Z is the final remaining count.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Fitness Log Step Goal Streak
tasks.prompt:
A fitness app tracks daily step counts over 12 days. A day is a "goal day" if steps are at least 8000. The app reports the longest consecutive streak of goal days and the total number of goal days.

The daily step counts (in order) are:
7500, 8200, 9100, 8800, 7900, 8500, 9200, 8700, 8300, 7800, 8100, 8600

Write a program that determines which days meet the goal, then outputs exactly two lines:
Goal days: X
Longest streak: Y
where X is the total count of goal days and Y is the length of the longest consecutive run of goal days.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Print Shop Color Sequence Changeover
tasks.prompt:
A print shop's press switches between 4 ink colors: C (cyan), M (magenta), Y (yellow), K (black). Each color change requires a cleaning cycle. The press starts on color C. Track how many cleaning cycles are needed for a sequence of print jobs.

The color required for each of 12 jobs (in order) is:
C, M, Y, K, C, M, M, Y, K, K, C, M

Rules:
- The press begins set to C.
- For each job, if the required color differs from the current color, increment the cleaning cycle count and change the current color to the required color.
- If the color matches, no cycle is needed.

Write a program that outputs exactly two lines:
Cycles: X
Final color: D
where X is the total number of cleaning cycles and D is the final color letter.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Museum Visitor Pair Search
tasks.prompt:
A museum records the number of visitors each hour from 10:00 to 15:00 (6 hours) as an array: [45, 38, 52, 47, 61, 33].

Write a program that finds the first adjacent pair of hours (consecutive entries) whose combined visitors equal exactly 100 or more, and also finds the last such pair.

Output exactly these 3 lines:
First pair: H1 H2 = S
Last pair: H1 H2 = S
Total pairs meeting goal: N

Where H1 and H2 are the 1-based hour indices, S is the sum of the two values, and N is the count of all adjacent pairs whose sum is 100 or more.

Example: if the first adjacent pair meeting the goal is hours 3 and 4 with sum 99, the line would read "First pair: 3 4 = 99" (adjust numbers as appropriate for the actual data).

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: School Cafeteria Lunch Line Windows
tasks.prompt:
A school cafeteria counts the number of students in line each minute for 10 minutes: [7, 9, 6, 12, 11, 8, 14, 10, 5, 9].

Write a program that examines every window of 3 consecutive minutes (minutes 1-3, 2-4, ..., 8-10) and reports:
- The window (by starting minute index, 1-based) with the maximum total.
- The window (by starting minute index, 1-based) with the minimum total.
- The number of windows whose total is 30 or more.

Output exactly these 3 lines:
Max window starts at: M with total T
Min window starts at: M with total T
Windows at or above 30: N

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: Recipe Book Oven Temperature Runs
tasks.prompt:
A recipe book logs oven temperatures (in Celsius) for 14 consecutive checks: [180, 185, 190, 190, 190, 175, 175, 200, 205, 205, 180, 180, 180, 180].

Write a program that finds:
- The longest run of consecutive identical temperatures. If there is a tie, report the earliest one.
- The temperature value of that run.
- The number of runs of length exactly 2.

Output exactly these 3 lines:
Longest run: value V length L
Run value: V
Runs of length 2: N

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: Mountain Hut Guest Bed Occupancy
tasks.prompt:
A mountain hut records how many of its 20 beds are occupied each night for 12 nights: [8, 14, 14, 14, 6, 11, 11, 17, 17, 17, 17, 9].

Write a program that finds:
- The first night (1-based) where occupancy reaches exactly 14 or more.
- The last night (1-based) where occupancy is strictly below 10.
- The longest consecutive streak of nights where occupancy is 11 or more (report its length).

Output exactly these 3 lines:
First night at 14+: N
Last night below 10: N
Longest streak at 11+: L

If a value is never found, print "none" instead of the number for that line.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: Garden Watering Moisture Scan
tasks.prompt:
A garden soil moisture sensor reports readings every hour for 10 hours: [42, 55, 61, 38, 45, 72, 68, 55, 33, 47].

Write a program that:
- Finds the first index (1-based) where the reading is greater than the reading immediately before it AND greater than the reading immediately after it (a local peak). Report the first such index and its value.
- Finds the longest consecutive run where readings are below 50. Report the run's starting index (1-based), its length, and its value at the start of the run.
- Counts how many readings are strictly between 40 and 60 inclusive.

Output exactly these 4 lines:
First peak: index I value V
Low run start: index I length L value V
Readings in [40,60]: N
Peak count: P

Where P is the total number of local peaks (indices 2 through 9 meeting the peak condition).

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: Museum Gift Shop Stock Scan
tasks.prompt:
A museum gift shop counts postcards on display each day for 10 days: [25, 31, 31, 18, 44, 44, 44, 44, 29, 37].

Write a program that finds:
- The first day (1-based) where the count exceeds 30.
- The last day (1-based) where the count is at most 30.
- The longest run of consecutive days with the same count (report the count value and run length; if tied, report the earliest).

Output exactly these 3 lines:
First day over 30: D
Last day at 30 or under: D
Longest same-count run: value V length L

If a value is never found, print "none" for that line.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: School Library Book Return Pairs
tasks.prompt:
A school library records the number of books returned each hour for 9 hours: [12, 8, 15, 22, 7, 19, 14, 6, 21].

Write a program that examines every pair of non-adjacent hours (i < j, j > i+1) and finds the pair whose sum is closest to 30 (without going over). If multiple pairs tie, report the one with the smallest i, then smallest j.

Also count how many pairs (adjacent or not, i < j) have a sum of exactly 30 or more.

Output exactly these 3 lines:
Best pair: H1 H2 = S
Pair sum: S
Pairs at 30+: N

Where H1 and H2 are 1-based indices of the two hours and S is their sum.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: Garden Greenhouse Humidity Scan
tasks.prompt:
A greenhouse humidity sensor reports percent values every 2 hours for 12 readings: [65, 72, 80, 80, 80, 58, 63, 71, 71, 85, 85, 60].

Write a program that:
- Finds the longest run of consecutive readings that are all at least 70. Report its starting index (1-based) and length. If there is a tie, report the earliest run.
- Finds the first index (1-based) where a reading drops below the previous reading.
- Counts readings that are strictly above 75.

Output exactly these 3 lines:
Longest run at 70+: start S length L
First drop at index: I
Readings above 75: N

If a drop never occurs, print "none" for that line's value. If no run meets the condition, print "none" for that line.

No trailing spaces.
tasks.category: searching and scanning arrays (pairs, windows of fixed size, longest runs, first/last occurrences)

tasks.title: Vending Machine Snack Selection
tasks.prompt:
A vending machine needs to display its top-selling snacks. You are given a list of snack names and their sales counts for the week. Use a selection sort to arrange the snacks by sales count in descending order. If two snacks have the same count, list them alphabetically by name.

Snacks and sales:
- Chips: 45
- Cookies: 45
- Pretzels: 30
- Crackers: 52
- Popcorn: 18

Print the top 3 snacks in the following format, one per line:
Rank 1: <name> (<count>)
Rank 2: <name> (<count>)
Rank 3: <name> (<count>)
tasks.category: sorting and selection written by hand (insertion, selection, counting sort; ranking with ties)

tasks.title: Weather Station Daily Highs
tasks.prompt:
A weather station records the daily high temperatures for a week in degrees Celsius. Use an insertion sort to arrange the temperatures in ascending order.

Temperatures: 21, 18, 24, 24, 19, 27, 22

Print the sorted temperatures on a single line, separated by a space, with each value shown as an integer. Then print a second line showing the median temperature as a Real with exactly one decimal place (for an even count, average the two middle values).
tasks.category: sorting and selection written by hand (insertion, selection, counting sort; ranking with ties)

tasks.title: School Library Book Due Dates
tasks.prompt:
A school library tracks the due dates of overdue books. A due date is represented as a text in YYYY-MM-DD format. Use a counting-style approach or simple sort to order the due dates from earliest to latest.

Due dates: 2024-03-15, 2024-01-22, 2024-03-15, 2024-02-10, 2024-01-22

Print each unique due date in order (earliest first), followed by the number of books due on that date, in this exact format:
<date>: <count> books
tasks.category: sorting and selection written by hand (insertion, selection, counting sort; ranking with ties)

tasks.title: Train Network Passenger Counts
tasks.prompt:
A train network counts the number of passengers boarding at each station during a single hour. Use a counting sort to arrange the stations by passenger count in ascending order.

Stations and counts:

tasks.title: Recipe Book Allergen Check
tasks.prompt:
A recipe book stores its recipes as a JSON document. The document contains a list of recipes. Each recipe has a "name" (Text), a "servings" (Int), and a "tags" list (array of Text).

The document is:

```json
{"recipes":[{"name":"Tomato Basil Soup","servings":4,"tags":["vegetarian","gluten-free"]},{"name":"Beef Stew","servings":6,"tags":["dairy-free"]},{"name":"Garden Salad","servings":2,"tags":["vegan","gluten-free","nut-free"]},{"name":"Cheese Omelette","servings":1,"tags":["vegetarian","gluten-free","nut-free"]},{"name":"Peanut Noodles","servings":3,"tags":["vegan","dairy-free"]}]}

Write a program that reads this JSON and prints a report. The report has exactly the following format:

1. The first line is: `TOTAL RECIPES: ` followed by the total number of recipes.

3. The third line is: `GLUTEN-FREE COUNT: ` followed by how many recipes have the tag `gluten-free`.
4. The fourth line is: `NUT-FREE COUNT: ` followed by how many recipes have the tag `nut-free`. If a recipe does not list this tag, it is not counted.

tasks.title: Bike Share Station Inventory
tasks.prompt:
A bike-share company tracks its stations in a JSON document. Each station has a `name` (Text), `bikes` (Int), and `capacity` (Int). Some stations may also have an optional `note` field.

{"stations":[{"name":"Harbor","bikes":12,"capacity":20},{"name":"Market","bikes":5,"capacity":15,"note":"under repair"},{"name":"Hilltop","bikes":0,"capacity":10},{"name":"Lakeside","bikes":18,"capacity":25},{"name":"Airport","bikes":7,"capacity":30,"note":"new dock"}]}

Write a program that reads this JSON and prints exactly the following report:

1. Line 1: `STATIONS: ` followed by the total number of stations.
2. Line 2: `EMPTY STATIONS: ` followed by the number of stations where `bikes` is 0.
3. Line 3: `TOTAL BIKES: ` followed by the sum of `bikes` across all stations.
4. Line 4: `TOTAL CAPACITY: ` followed by the sum of `capacity` across all stations.
5. Line 5: `FILL RATE: ` followed by `TOTAL BIKES` divided by `TOTAL CAPACITY`, printed with exactly 3 decimal places.
6. Lines 6 through N: for every station that has a `note` field, print `NOTE: ` followed by the station name, a space, a colon, a space, and the note text. Print these lines in the order the stations appear in the document.

Print no trailing spaces.

tasks.title: Orchard Harvest Yield

tasks.title: Recipe Book Missing Ingredients

tasks.prompt:

Line 8: `Worst overdue lamp: ` followed by the lamp number of the oldest overdue record, or `0` if there are none.
Line 9: `Worst hours: ` followed by the hours of that record formatted to exactly 3 decimal places, or `0.000` if there are none.

A print shop stores job metadata in a JSON object. Each key is a job code and the value is a JSON value of varying type.

The JSON content is:

```
{
  "J101": 42,
  "J102": "rush",
  "J103": 3.75,
  "J104": true,
  "J105": 17,
  "J106": "standard",
  "J107": false,
  "J108": 8.2
}
```

Write a program that prints one line per key (in the order shown above) showing the type of the value. Use these labels:

- Integers print as `int`
- Reals print as `real`
- Booleans print as `bool`
- Texts print as `text`

The format for each line is:

`<key>: <type>`

Output exactly 8 lines in the order the keys appear above. Use no trailing spaces.
tasks.category: converting between a JSON document and formatted text output (tables, key paths, type checks of mixed values)

tasks.title: Board Game Score Summary Table
tasks.prompt:
A board game night stores results in a JSON array. Each entry has `player` (Text), `round1` (Int), and `round2` (Int).

The JSON content is:

```
[
  {"player": "Alice", "round1": 12, "round2": 15},
  {"player": "Bob", "round1": 18, "round2": 9},
  {"player": "Carol", "round1": 7, "round2": 14},
  {"player": "Dave", "round1": 21, "round2": 6}
]
```

Write a program that prints a table. First print a header line:

`Player   R1   R2   Total`

Then for each player (in the order given), print a line where the name is left-aligned in 8 characters, `R1` and `R2` are right-aligned in 4 characters, and `Total` is right-aligned in 6 characters. `Total` is `round1 + round2`.

Output exactly 5 lines. Use no trailing spaces (the last column may end at the final digit of `Total`).
tasks.category: converting between a JSON document and formatted text output (tables, key paths, type checks of mixed values)

tasks.title: Museum Artifact Field Checker
tasks.prompt:
A museum stores artifact records in a JSON array. Each record has `name` (Text), `origin` (Text), and `weight_kg` (Real).

The JSON content is:

```
[
  {"name": "Amphora", "origin": "Greece", "weight_kg": 3.4},
  {"name": "Scroll", "origin": "Egypt", "weight_kg": 0.2},
  {"name": "Coin", "origin": "Rome", "weight_kg": 0.01},
  {"name": "Mask", "origin": "Mexico", "weight_kg": 1.15},
  {"name": "Idol", "origin": "Peru", "weight_kg": 2.7}
]
```

Write a program that prints one line per artifact showing whether it is heavier than 1 kg. The format is:

`<name> from <origin>: <heavy|light>`

where `<heavy|light>` is `heavy` if `weight_kg` is strictly greater than 1.0, otherwise `light`.

Output exactly 5 lines in the order given. Use no trailing spaces.

tasks.title: Print Shop Color Swatch Sort
tasks.prompt:
A print shop stores color swatches in a JSON array. Each swatch has `name` (Text), `r` (Int), `g` (Int), `b` (Int).

The JSON content is:

```

Write a program that computes each swatch's brightness as `(r + g + b) / 3` (a Real) and prints one line per swatch in the format:

tasks.title: Orchard Fruit Ripeness Check
tasks.prompt:
You are given a JSON document representing an orchard harvest log. It contains a list of fruit batches, each with fields: `fruit` (Text), `ripeness` (Int, 1-10), `weight_kg` (Real), and `tree_id` (Text).

The orchard JSON is:
```json
{
  "orchard": "Green Valley",
  "batches": [
    {"fruit": "apple", "ripeness": 8, "weight_kg": 145.6, "tree_id": "A1"},
    {"fruit": "pear", "ripeness": 5, "weight_kg": 88.3, "tree_id": "B2"},
    {"fruit": "apple", "ripeness": 3, "weight_kg": 112.4, "tree_id": "A2"},
    {"fruit": "cherry", "ripeness": 9, "weight_kg": 45.7, "tree_id": "C1"},
    {"fruit": "pear", "ripeness": 7, "weight_kg": 96.1, "tree_id": "B1"},
    {"fruit": "apple", "ripeness": 6, "weight_kg": 130.9, "tree_id": "A3"}
  ]
}
```

Write a program that reads this JSON and prints a ripeness report in the following exact format (5 lines):

Line 1: `Batches: N` where N is the total number of batches.
Line 2: `Ripe Batches: R` where R is the number of batches with `ripeness` >= 7.
Line 3: `Total Weight: W` where W is the sum of all `weight_kg` values formatted to exactly 1 decimal place.
Line 4: `Top Batch: T` where T is the `tree_id` of the batch with the highest `ripeness` value.
Line 5: `Apple Count: C` where C is the number of batches where `fruit` is `apple`.

There must be no trailing spaces on any line.

tasks.title: Bakery Daily Order Totals
tasks.prompt:
You are given a JSON document representing a bakery's daily orders. It contains a list of orders, each with fields: `order_id` (Text), `items` (Int), `unit_price` (Real), and `paid` (Bool).

The bakery JSON is:
```json
{
  "bakery": "Sweet Crumbs",
  "orders": [
    {"order_id": "ORD-001", "items": 3, "unit_price": 4.50, "paid": true},
    {"order_id": "ORD-002", "items": 5, "unit_price": 3.75, "paid": true},
    {"order_id": "ORD-003", "items": 2, "unit_price": 6.25, "paid": false},
    {"order_id": "ORD-004", "items": 8, "unit_price": 2.99, "paid": true},
    {"order_id": "ORD-005", "items": 4, "unit_price": 5.00, "paid": false},
    {"order_id": "ORD-006", "items": 6, "unit_price": 4.25, "paid": true}
  ]
}
```

Write a program that reads this JSON and prints an order report in the following exact format (6 lines):

Line 1: `Orders: N` where N is the total number of orders.
Line 2: `Paid Total: P` where P is the sum of `items * unit_price` for all orders where `paid` is true, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 3: `Unpaid Total: U` where U is the sum of `items * unit_price` for all orders where `paid` is false, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 4: `Largest Order: O` where O is the `order_id` of the order with the greatest `items` value.
Line 5: `Avg Order Value: A` where A is the average of `items * unit_price` across ALL orders, formatted to exactly 2 decimal places.
Line 6: `Items Sold: S` where S is the sum of `items` for all paid orders only.

There must be no trailing spaces on any line.

{

tasks.title: Coffee Shop Daily Receipts
tasks.prompt:
You are given a JSON document representing a coffee shop's daily receipts. It contains a list of transactions, each with fields: `receipt_id` (Text), `item` (Text), `price` (Real), `quantity` (Int), and `discount_pct` (Int, percentage off, 0 means no discount).

The receipts JSON is:
```json
{
  "shop": "Bean There",
  "receipts": [
    {"receipt_id": "R01", "item": "Latte", "price": 4.50, "quantity": 2, "discount_pct": 0},
    {"receipt_id": "R02", "item": "Muffin", "price": 3.25, "quantity": 1, "discount_pct": 10},
    {"receipt_id": "R03", "item": "Latte", "price": 4.50, "quantity": 3, "discount_pct": 0},
    {"receipt_id": "R04", "item": "Croissant", "price": 3.75, "quantity": 2, "discount_pct": 20},
    {"receipt_id": "R05", "item": "Muffin", "price": 3.25, "quantity": 4, "discount_pct": 0},
    {"receipt_id": "R06", "item": "Croissant", "price": 3.75, "quantity": 1, "discount_pct": 0}
  ]
}
```

Write a program that reads this JSON and prints a receipts report in the following exact format (6 lines):

Line 1: `Receipts: N` where N is the total number of receipts.

tasks.title: Florist Bouquet Order Report
tasks.prompt:

- `flowers` (Int): number of flowers in the bouquet
- `ribbon` (Text): the ribbon color, one of "red", "blue", "white"
- `customer` (Text): customer name
- `express` (Bool): true if the order is express (rush)

Write a program that reads `bouquets.json` and prints the following report, each line exactly as shown (no trailing spaces):

```
Florist Bouquet Order Report
Total orders: <N>
Express orders: <E>
Average flowers: <A with 2 decimal places>
Most flowers: <order id>
Ribbon counts: red=<R> blue=<B> white=<W>
```

- `<N>` is the total number of orders.
- `<E>` is the number of orders where `express` is true.
- `<A>` is the average `flowers` across all orders, printed with exactly 2 decimal places (no rounding ambiguity in the data).
- `<order id>` is the `order` id of the order with the highest `flowers` value; if there is a tie, print the one that appears first in the file.

tasks.title: Community Center Class Enrollment

- `enrolled` (Int): number of enrolled students
- `capacity` (Int): maximum capacity

Art enrolled: <A>

tasks.title: Laundry Room Dryer Cycle Monitor
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program to monitor a shared laundry room dryer. The dryer has four settings: "Delicates" (dries for 40 minutes), "Cotton" (dries for 60 minutes), "Permanent Press" (dries for 50 minutes), and "Towels" (dries for 70 minutes). The dryer is started by a button press that selects a setting in a fixed order (Delicates -> Cotton -> Permanent Press -> Towels -> Delicates -> ...). A second button press starts the cycle for the currently selected setting. While a cycle is running, a "remaining" counter counts down by 10 minutes per tick until it reaches 0, at which point the dryer beeps and the selected setting resets to the first setting (Delicates).

The input is a fixed sequence of 14 events:
["SELECT", "SELECT", "START", "TICK", "TICK", "TICK", "TICK", "TICK", "TICK", "TICK", "TICK", "SELECT", "START", "TICK"]

Initially the dryer is idle and the selected setting is "Delicates". A "SELECT" event advances the selected setting by one step in the order. A "START" event begins a cycle for the current setting if the dryer is idle (otherwise it does nothing). A "TICK" event reduces remaining time by 10 minutes if a cycle is running (otherwise it does nothing).

Output exactly 4 lines in this format (no trailing spaces):
LastSetting: <setting name>
LastDuration: <integer minutes>
Remaining: <integer minutes>
Beeps: <integer>

Where:
- LastSetting is the name of the setting of the most recently started cycle.
- LastDuration is the total duration in minutes of the most recently started cycle.
- Remaining is the remaining minutes on the dryer after the last event (0 if idle).
- Beeps is how many times the dryer beeped (reached 0) during the entire sequence.

tasks.title: Elevator Floor Request Sequencer
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program for a small office elevator that services floors 1 through 6. The elevator starts on floor 1, doors closed, and idle. It receives a fixed sequence of 16 events:
["CALL:3", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:5", "CALL:5", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:2", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:6", "CALL:6", "CALL:6", "OPEN", "CLOSE", "CALL:4"]

The events work as follows:
- "CALL:n" adds floor n to the request queue if it is not already in the queue (duplicates are ignored). If the elevator is idle and the queue is non-empty, the elevator immediately begins moving toward the first floor in the queue, one floor per tick, until it reaches it; upon arrival the elevator becomes "waiting" (doors still closed) until an OPEN event.
- "OPEN" opens the doors if the elevator is waiting at a requested floor; this removes that floor from the queue and the elevator becomes "idle". If the elevator is not waiting, OPEN does nothing.
- "CLOSE" closes the doors if they are open; otherwise does nothing.

When the elevator finishes moving to a floor and becomes "waiting", it does NOT automatically process further CALL events until an OPEN/CLOSE cycle occurs.

Output exactly 5 lines (no trailing spaces):
FinalFloor: <integer>
Doors: <Open or Closed>
QueueLength: <integer>
TotalFloorsTraveled: <integer>
VisitedFloors: <comma-separated floors in order visited, e.g. 3,5,2>

VisitedFloors lists each floor the elevator arrived at (became waiting at) in chronological order, including repeats.
tasks.category: finite state machines processing a fixed input sequence

tasks.title: Coffee Shop Order State Tracker
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program that tracks the state of orders at a small coffee shop counter. Each order goes through states in this fixed cycle: "Received" -> "Making" -> "Ready" -> "PickedUp" (then the order is done and removed). Only one order can be in the "Making" state at a time; if a second order tries to enter "Making" while another is making, it stays in "Received".

The shop receives a fixed sequence of 18 events:
["NEW:A", "NEW:B", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "NEW:C", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "NEW:D", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "NEW:E", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE", "ADVANCE"]

- "NEW:x" creates a new order with id x in state "Received" and appends it to the back of the queue.
- "ADVANCE" moves the front-most order that can advance one step: if the front order is "Received" and nothing is "Making", it becomes "Making"; if the front order is "Making", it becomes "Ready"; if the front order is "Ready", it becomes "PickedUp" and is removed. If no order can advance, ADVANCE does nothing.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):
Queue: <comma-separated order ids in queue order, or EMPTY>
FrontState: <state of the front order, or NONE>
Making: <order id currently Making, or NONE>
PickedUpCount: <integer>

PickedUpCount is how many orders reached "PickedUp" during the whole sequence.

tasks.title: Robot Vacuum Room Sweep Log

The vacuum receives a fixed sequence of 20 commands:
["MOVE", "CLEAN", "MOVE", "MOVE", "CLEAN", "MOVE", "MOVE", "CLEAN", "TURN", "MOVE", "CLEAN", "MOVE", "CLEAN", "MOVE", "MOVE", "CLEAN", "MOVE", "CLEAN", "MOVE", "CLEAN"]

- "MOVE" advances the vacuum one tile in its current direction. If it would move off either end (below 0 or above 7), it instead turns around (reverses direction) and stays in place.
- "CLEAN" reduces the dust level of the current tile by 2, but not below 0.
- "TURN" reverses the direction.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):
FinalTile: <integer>
Direction: <Left or Right>
DustLeft: <comma-separated dust levels for tiles 0..7>
TotalCleaned: <integer>

TotalCleaned is the sum of dust removed across all CLEAN commands (each removal counts how much was actually subtracted).

tasks.title: Laundromat Dryer Door Interlock Check

Rules:
- "CLOSE_DOOR" sets DoorClosed to true.
- "OPEN_DOOR" sets DoorClosed to false; if DrumRotating is true at that moment, it also forces DrumRotating to false (emergency stop) and increments a violation counter.
- "START" sets DrumRotating to true only if DoorClosed is true; otherwise it does nothing.
- "STOP" sets DrumRotating to false.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):

DrumRotating: <true or false>

StartsWhileClosed counts how many START events successfully began rotation.

tasks.title: Board Game Turn Phase Tracker

The game receives a fixed sequence of 18 events:

- The current phase starts at "Draw" for Player 1.
- "DRAW" advances Draw->Play, "PLAY" advances Play->Score, "SCORE" advances Score->End, "END" advances End->next player's Draw.
- If an event does not match the current phase, it is ignored (no state change).
- When "END" is processed, the current player is recorded as having completed a turn, and the player switches (1->2, 2->1).

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):

tasks.title: Vending Machine Service Mode Log
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program for a vending machine that can enter a service mode. The machine has states: "Normal", "Service", "Error". It starts in "Normal". It processes a fixed sequence of 16 events:
["CODE", "CODE", "ENTER", "STOCK", "STOCK", "EXIT", "CODE", "ENTER", "STOCK", "JAM", "CODE", "ENTER", "EXIT", "VEND", "VEND", "CODE"]

Rules:
- "CODE" (pressing the service code button): if in "Normal", it starts a code-entry counter at 1; if the counter reaches 2 consecutively, the machine enters "Service" and the counter resets. If in "Service", "CODE" does nothing. If in "Error", "CODE" resets the machine to "Normal" and clears the counter.
- "ENTER": if in "Service", does nothing (already in). If in "Normal", ignored.
- "STOCK": if in "Service", increments stockCount by 1; otherwise ignored.
- "EXIT": if in "Service", returns to "Normal"; otherwise ignored.
- "JAM": if in "Service" or "Normal", moves to "Error"; stockCount is preserved.
- "VEND": if in "Normal", increments vendCount by 1; otherwise ignored.

The code-entry counter only increments on consecutive CODE events; any other event resets it to 0.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):
FinalState: <Normal or Service or Error>
StockCount: <integer>
VendCount: <integer>
ServiceEntries: <integer>

ServiceEntries counts how many times the machine transitioned into "Service".

Rules:
- "NEXT" moves one stop in the current direction. If it would go past either end (index < 0 or > 5), the bus stays put and reverses direction instead.
- "OPEN" opens doors only if closed; "CLOSE" closes doors only if open. Opening at a stop records a visit to that stop name (appended to a visit log).

tasks.title: Photocopier Job Queue State
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program that tracks a photocopier's job queue. Jobs arrive with an id and page count. The copier processes one job at a time in FIFO order. It receives a fixed sequence of 14 events:
["JOB:J1:10", "JOB:J2:5", "START", "RUN", "RUN", "RUN", "START", "JOB:J3:8", "RUN", "RUN", "RUN", "RUN", "START", "RUN"]

Rules:
- "JOB:id:pages" enqueues a job (id, pages) at the back of the queue.
- "START" begins processing the front job if the copier is idle (state "Idle" -> "Busy"). If a job is already busy, START does nothing. If the queue is empty, START does nothing.
- "RUN" processes 3 pages from the current job if Busy (pages remaining -= 3, but not below 0). If the job reaches 0 pages remaining, it completes: record its id in a completed list, the copier returns to "Idle", and RUN does nothing further this event.

Output exactly 4 lines (no trailing spaces):
Queue: <comma-separated job ids waiting, or EMPTY>
Completed: <comma-separated completed job ids in order, or NONE>
PagesRemaining: <pages left on the currently processing job, or 0 if idle>

TotalPagesDone is the sum of pages actually processed across all RUN events.

tasks.title: Smart Thermostat Mode Cycle
tasks.prompt:
You are writing a program for a home thermostat with modes cycled by a single button: "Off" -> "Heat" -> "Cool" -> "Auto" -> "Off" -> ... It starts in "Off". It also has a hold flag (Bool, initially false) and a target temperature (Int, initially 20).

It receives a fixed sequence of 16 events:
["MODE", "MODE", "HOLD", "UP", "UP", "MODE", "HOLD", "DOWN", "MODE", "MODE", "UP", "HOLD", "MODE", "DOWN", "DOWN", "MODE"]

Rules:
- "MODE" advances to the next mode in the cycle, EXCEPT if hold is true, in which case MODE is ignored.
- "HOLD" toggles the hold flag (true<->false).

Each booking occupies end minus start hours. Compute:
- totalBookings: the number of bookings across all lanes.
- totalHours: the sum of hours occupied across all bookings.
- emptyLanes: the number of lanes whose bookings array is empty.
- mastersHours: the total hours booked by the group "Masters Swim".
- busiestLane: the lane number with the most total hours (data chosen so there is a unique maximum).

Print exactly these 6 lines, no trailing spaces:
Pool: Riverside Pool
Total bookings: <totalBookings>
Total hours: <totalHours>
Empty lanes: <emptyLanes>
Masters Swim hours: <mastersHours>
Busiest lane: <busiestLane>

tasks.prompt:

- `category` (Text): one of "bread", "pastry", or "cake".
- `ingredients` (Array of Text): list of ingredient names used.
- `sold` (Bool): whether the item sold out.

Write a program that reads `bakery.json` and prints the following report, with each section separated by a blank line:

Section 1 - counts per category, in this exact order and format:
`bread: <count>`
`pastry: <count>`
`cake: <count>`

Section 2 - ingredient usage. Collect every ingredient from every item, count how many times each distinct ingredient appears, then print each ingredient and its count sorted alphabetically by ingredient name, in this format:

Section 3 - a single line:
`Sold out: <count>`
where `<count>` is how many items have `sold` set to true.

tasks.title: Train Network On-Time Ranking
tasks.prompt:
You are analyzing train punctuality. You are given a JSON file named `trains.json` containing a list of train services. Each service is a JSON object with these fields:
- `service_id` (Text): unique identifier like "S1".
- `line` (Text): the line name, e.g. "North", "South", "East", "West".
- `scheduled` (Int): scheduled arrival time in minutes after midnight.
- `actual` (Int, optional): actual arrival time in minutes after midnight. Absent if the service was cancelled.

Write a program that reads `trains.json` and prints the following report:

Line 1: `Cancelled: <count>` where `<count>` is the number of services missing the `actual` field.

Then a blank line.

Then, for every non-cancelled service, compute `delay = actual - scheduled`. Print only services whose delay is greater than 0, sorted by delay descending (largest delay first; if two services have the same delay, sort by `service_id` ascending). Each line in this exact format:
`<service_id> | <line> | delay: <delay> min`

Then a blank line.

Last line: `Worst delay: <service_id>` where `<service_id>` is the service with the largest delay (ties broken by smallest `service_id`).

Do not print any trailing spaces.
tasks.category: reading a small JSON data file provided with the exercise and reporting from it (records with optional fields, grouping, ranking)

tasks.title: Orchard Harvest Weight Report
tasks.prompt:
You manage an orchard and need a harvest report. You are given a JSON file named `harvest.json` containing a list of harvest crates. Each crate is a JSON object with these fields:
- `crate_id` (Text): unique identifier like "C01".
- `variety` (Text): apple variety name.
- `weight_kg` (Real): weight of the crate in kilograms.
- `grade` (Text, optional): quality grade, either "A" or "B". May be absent if not yet graded.

Write a program that reads `harvest.json` and prints the following report, with sections separated by blank lines:

Section 1: `Unguarded: <count>` where `<count>` is the number of crates missing the `grade` field.

Section 2: `Total weight: <total>` where `<total>` is the sum of all `weight_kg` values, printed with exactly 1 decimal place.

Section 3: For each variety that appears, print a line sorted alphabetically by variety name, in this exact format:
`<variety>: <crate_count> crates, <avg_weight> kg avg`
where `<crate_count>` is how many crates have that variety, and `<avg_weight>` is the average `weight_kg` of those crates printed with exactly 1 decimal place.

Section 4: Print the single crate with the highest `weight_kg` (if tied, the one that appears first in the file), in this exact format:
`Heaviest: <crate_id> (<weight_kg> kg)` with `weight_kg` printed with exactly 1 decimal place.

Choose your data so no average or total falls exactly halfway when rounded to 1 decimal place. Do not print any trailing spaces.
tasks.category: reading a small JSON data file provided with the exercise and reporting from it (records with optional fields, grouping, ranking)

tasks.title: Museum Visitor Attendance Log
tasks.prompt:
You work at a museum and need to analyze visitor attendance. You are given a JSON file named `visitors.json` containing a list of daily attendance records. Each record is a JSON object with these fields:
- `day` (Text): day of the week, e.g. "Mon", "Tue".
- `visitors` (Int): total number of visitors that day.
- `exhibit` (Text): the most popular exhibit that day.
- `members` (Int, optional): number of those visitors who were members. Absent for some days.

Write a program that reads `visitors.json` and prints the following report:

Line 1: `Days logged: <count>`

Then a blank line.

Then, for each day in the order they appear in the file, print a line in this exact format:
`<day>: <visitors> visitors, <exhibit>`

Then a blank line.

Then `Member share: <share>` where `<share>` is the total of all `members` values divided by the total of all `visitors` values, printed as a percentage with exactly 1 decimal place followed by a percent sign, e.g. `42.3%`. Days missing the `members` field contribute 0 to the members total but still contribute their `visitors` to the visitors total.

Then a blank line.

Last line: `Top exhibit: <exhibit>` where `<exhibit>` is the exhibit name that appears on the day with the most visitors (if tied, the exhibit from the earliest such day in the file).

Choose your data so the percentage does not fall exactly halfway when rounded. Do not print any trailing spaces.

tasks.title: Fitness Studio Class Capacity Grid
tasks.prompt:
A fitness studio has a 4x5 grid of class slots. Each slot holds the number of enrolled members (0 to 30). Capacity per slot is 20.
The grid is:
Row1: 18 22 15 20 12
Row2: 25 19 21 17 14
Row3: 11 23 16 24 13
Row4: 20 18 22 19 10

A slot is 'over' if enrolled > 20, 'full' if enrolled == 20, 'under' if enrolled < 20.
Utilization = 100 * total enrolled / (20 * 20), rounded to 1 decimal place.

Produce the report exactly as shown:
Over capacity: <count>
Exactly full: <count>
Under capacity: <count>
Total enrolled: <sum>
Utilization: <value>%

Print counts and total as plain integers. Utilization printed with 1 decimal place followed by a percent sign, no space; never exactly .X5.
